findings.observed: try_wait ? executes before handling already-observed output error. A simultaneous try_wait error returns Err, skipping queued tail delivery, Failed terminal and direct-child cancel attempt. UI catches error and clears local active state while HOST lease has no terminal to reconcile.
findings.reproduce: ProcessPort scripted try_read => stdout tail + stdout_completion Error, stderr Eof; try_wait => PortError::Process. Call live poll once: current returns Err instead of chunks followed by Failed; run remains unfinished. Source control flow proof; independent executable regression requested from test owner.
findings.classification: Pre-existing plain wait-error behavior is a follow-up; new read-error precedence/terminal promise bypass is in current approved scope.
findings.minimal_fix: Classify known output read error before fallible try_wait, or retain wait result without overriding read-error terminal; preserve primary read error and captured tail, no new public API.
findings.fix: Known read-error classification now precedes wait failure propagation; simultaneous wait error appended, captured tail returned before one Failed, direct child cancel attempted once.

independent_evidence.red: ../process-tests/exec-r1-red.txt: one test compiled then failed intended naked wait Err instead of Failed event

conformance.ports: Only approved StreamCompletion enum, two ProcessOutput fields and one re-export. Trait signatures/is_empty data-only unchanged.
conformance.dependencies: No new crate/trait/Manager; EXEC consumes ProcessPort, adapters own OS resources.
conformance.reader: Per-stream shared bytes/completion mutex, sticky EOF/error, Interrupted retried; try_read locks both before draining so poison does not discard healthy bytes. No reader joins in polling.
conformance.lifecycle: Observed exit stored once; deadline never reset on data; independent EOF/error observations; chunks before exactly one terminal including simultaneous stream-read/wait error. Plain wait-only error behavior unchanged, classified follow-up.
conformance.host: cancel_run request-only does not consume events; poll reconciles lease only on terminal.
conformance.ui: Empty batch continues; cancellation retains generation/run ID; terminal board may clear run ID but guarded continuation still finishes actual terminal. Late cancel ACK ignored after active ID changed.
conformance.scope: Actual pre-process-app.js byte-mask comparison: all bytes outside pollRunStream/cmdCancelRun exactly preserved.

policy_clarification.deadline: Implementation samples available states first and dual EOF wins at any poll, including >2000ms. Packet boundary_order explicitly says capture first then dual EOF completes; no reader timestamps or unattended timer were approved. This is observed-poll deadline, not proof actual reader completion took <=2s. Root notified to state this clearly; no new timestamp framework recommended.

followups.behavior: Second Assign increments runPollGeneration before HOST Busy rejection and catch clears activeRunId. Existing run UI polling may be invalidated although HOST retains lease. Same code verified in pre-process snapshot.
followups.action: Separate bounded UI guard task; do not opportunistically edit current slice.

followups.behavior: StdProcess cancel ignores native kill/wait errors; current approved scope retains existing behavior. No process-tree containment/reaping guarantee.
ProcessPort plain try_wait error with no known output-read error still returns ExecError; broader host/UI recovery not changed by this bounded readerror fix.
